pages.text: A chiral catalyst lowers the barrier to one mirror-image product by ΔΔG‡ more than to the other, so one forms e^(ΔΔG‡/RT) times faster: the enantiomeric excess is ee = (s − 1)/(s + 1). Colder gives a purer product, but every rate follows Arrhenius, and falls.
$(thing)Set$(): Reaction temperature, Hydrogen pressure.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Catalyst ageing: the barrier difference varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Too much hydrogen: the catalyst is stripped.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Warmer and higher pressure are faster, but less selective.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Selectivity: s = e^(ΔΔG‡/RT)$(br)Enantiomeric excess: ee = (s − 1)/(s + 1)$(br)Rate: k ∝ e^(−Ea/RT)·p
